text: Medium is Latin for in between and a medium can be seen as a mediator. <break time="0.8s" /> Something that enables communication across time and space. <break time="0.8s" /> Media are the material aspects of human communication. <break time="0.8s" /> News informs us about recent events. <break time="0.8s" /> Literature can provide existential insights. <break time="0.8s" /> Architecture not only provides shelter. <break time="0.8s" /> But also communicates social power relations. <break time="0.8s" /> Fashion communicates. <break time="0.8s" /> Ideas about the human body and about social norms. <break time="0.8s" /> In the 1960s. <break time="0.8s" /> Marshall McLuhan was already defining medium. <break time="0.8s" /> As any extension of man. <break time="0.8s" /> Thus the list of material objects that can function as a medium. <break time="0.8s" /> Is endless. <break time="0.8s" /> And it involves even. <break time="0.8s" /> Other physical phenomena like light or sound waves. <break time="0.8s" /> And our own bodies. <break time="0.8s" /> In other words. <break time="0.8s" /> Once we become interested. <break time="0.8s" /> In the material aspect of human communication. <break time="0.8s" /> Media suddenly turn out to be everywhere. <break time="0.8s" /> And anything and everything. <break time="0.8s" /> Can be used as a medium. <break time="0.8s" /> White pebbles on a beach. <break time="0.8s" /> Are not usually a medium. <break time="0.8s" /> But the white stones. <break time="0.8s" /> That Hansel, in the fairy tale by the Brothers Grimm, drops. <break time="0.8s" /> As he goes into the woods. <break time="0.8s" /> Are definitely a media product. <break time="0.8s" /> Conveying a simple but important message. <break time="0.8s" /> We came this way.
